jordan: Heads-up — saw a short-lived CPU spike during tokenization on an H100 batch yesterday. Not sure whether it's kv cache-related or a memcpy regression. Can someone run a short nsys + torchprof capture with prefix cache enabled?

jordan: Quick repro I ran locally (feel free to adapt):
```
nsys profile -o /tmp/trace --trace=cuda,osrt --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi:0-120 python -m infra.infer --model mixtral-8x7b --batch 2 --seq-len 256

# torch profiler snippet to export chrome trace
python - <<'PY'
from torch.profiler import profile, ProfilerActivity, schedule
def run_inference():
    # small loop calling runtime client
    pass
with profile(activities=[ProfilerActivity.CPU, ProfilerActivity.CUDA], schedule=schedule(wait=0,warmup=1,active=2), record_shapes=True) as p:
    run_inference()
    p.export_chrome_trace('/tmp/torchprof.json')
PY
```

jordan: Please scrub PII and upload to gs://redwood-profiles/eng-runtime/2046000001-jordan/ (use scripts/scrub-trace.sh).

sophia: I can take it. Will run on h100-lowlat-3, enabling `--kv-prefix=on` and `--seq-threshold=16`. I'll use 4 short prompts (non-sensitive) and attach metadata (git sha, driver, cuda). ETA ~30m.

perf-bot: Note: last clean H100 baseline for mixtral-8x7b: 2025-10-19 22:10 UTC — median token latency 2.0ms. Baseline tag: h100-mixtral-20251019 (id: daf456).

lee: Quick scrub tip: remove prompt text with `jq` from torchprof json or sed for logs. Also watch for presence of local paths in `args` fields.

matt: If you see CPU spikes tied to prepare/encode stages, check tokenizer caching and whether we accidentally disabled fastpath BPE. Also re-check `--force-pinned` defaults after recent change db4f2e.

sophia: Running captures now. Using slot h100-lowlat-3, capture range shortened to avoid huge files. Will upload zipped traces after scrub.

sophia: Done upload: gs://redwood-profiles/eng-runtime/2046000001-sophia/trace.zip (scrubbed). Added metadata.txt with git sha and `nvidia-smi` output. perf-bot, please run quick flamegraph + KV hit analysis.

perf-bot: Flamegraph queued for 2046000001-sophia. KV cache summary job started. Expect results in ~3m.

sophia: Flamegraph link: https://prof.redwood.internal/flame/2046000001-sophia.svg — shows memcpy spikes around attention + token-encoder. KV hit ratio reported at 0.18. Attached kv_stats.txt in bucket.

jordan: Low KV hit ratio makes sense for the short prompts; but the memcpy/attention timing looks suspicious for a pinned-memory regression. Can someone grep for `pinned` references or `cudaHostAlloc` calls in the trace?

lee: Helpful grep: `jq -r '.traceEvents[] | select(.name=="cudaMemcpy") | .args' torchprof.json` then search for host pointers. For nsys raw: `nsys stats --report gputrace /tmp/trace.qdrep` and look at `memcpy` buckets.

matt: Also check batchifier fallback logs — when fallback occurs we see extra synchronous copies. I can check the recent batchifier changes later today.

jordan: Sophia — can you open a minimal PR with the repro script and the perf check that asserts kv_hit_ratio > 0.5 for longer sequences? That will help CI catch regressions.

sophia: Opening PR now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8790 — branch perf/204600-kv-prefetch. Includes repro, upload links, and a short runbook for reviewers.

matt: Adding comment on PR: please validate `--force-pinned` interaction and include `nvidia-smi topo --matrix` in metadata. Assigning to kernel folks if memcpy hotspot persists.

jordan: After PR merges, let's re-run benchmark on A100 and H100 and mark against baseline. Thanks all :rocket:
